summary:
SpaceFarm is an educational RPG focused on exploring Mars and understanding the challenges of establishing sustainable human life beyond Earth. The game combines exploration, interactive activities, and educational content to introduce players to the science and technology behind living in extraterrestrial environments.

Its main objective is to spark curiosity among younger generations and encourage interest in space exploration, agricultural technology, and sustainable resource management. Through gameplay, players discover concepts such as crop cultivation, resource conservation, environmental adaptation, and the systems needed to support life on Mars.

Rather than relying only on theoretical explanations, SpaceFarm integrates scientific information into its activities, allowing players to explore these concepts through an interactive experience. The project shows how scientific knowledge and technological innovation can help address the challenges of future space missions.

The current version provides a foundation for further development. Future improvements will focus on expanding gameplay, strengthening educational content, improving the game's structure, and ensuring that the information presented is scientifically accurate and realistic.

Ultimately, SpaceFarm aims to make science more accessible and engaging, inspiring younger generations to learn about sustainable living beyond Earth and the future of space exploration.(Please increase video quality to 1080p)

SPACEFARM

NASA Space Apps Challenge — Project Documentation

Project Name: SpaceFarm
Project Focus: Space Exploration, Agriculture, Scientific Education, and Sustainability.
Programming Languages: HTML and JavaScript.
Development Tools: ChatGPT, CloudAI, Aseprite Pixel Art Editor, and cloud-based tools.

1. Project Overview

SpaceFarm is an educational video game designed to introduce younger generations to the scientific principles behind space exploration, extraterrestrial agriculture, and sustainable resource management.

As humanity continues to investigate the possibility of establishing a long-term presence beyond Earth, understanding how to produce food, manage essential resources, and maintain suitable living conditions in extraterrestrial environments becomes increasingly important.

However, many of these scientific concepts remain unfamiliar to younger audiences, particularly because they are often presented through complex technical explanations rather than accessible educational experiences.

SpaceFarm seeks to address this challenge by transforming scientific knowledge into an interactive learning experience.

Through immersive gameplay, players explore simulated extraterrestrial environments, develop agricultural systems, manage resources, and confront challenges inspired by the conditions that future space missions may encounter.

By combining entertainment with scientific education, SpaceFarm aims to make complex concepts more understandable while encouraging curiosity, experimentation, and critical thinking.

Our ultimate objective is to demonstrate that video games can serve as valuable educational tools capable of inspiring the next generation of scientists, engineers, researchers, and space explorers.

2. Problem Statement

One of the challenges facing scientific education is making complex subjects accessible and engaging to younger generations.

Topics such as planetary science, extraterrestrial agriculture, environmental sustainability, and space technology can be difficult to understand without practical examples or opportunities for experimentation.

Traditional educational methods often rely on theoretical explanations, which may limit students' ability to visualize how scientific concepts apply to real-world challenges.

Furthermore, as space agencies continue researching technologies that could support future human exploration of the Moon and Mars, there is an increasing opportunity to introduce students to the scientific challenges associated with living beyond Earth.

These challenges include limited water availability, extreme temperatures, atmospheric differences, radiation exposure, energy requirements, and the development of sustainable food production systems.

SpaceFarm addresses this educational opportunity by providing an interactive environment where players can explore these challenges through gameplay.

Rather than simply memorizing information, players are encouraged to understand scientific relationships, evaluate possible solutions, and recognize the importance of technological innovation in future space exploration.

3. Project Objectives

The primary objective of SpaceFarm is to promote scientific literacy through an accessible and engaging educational video game.

By combining space exploration with agricultural science, we aim to introduce players to the fundamental principles involved in sustaining human life beyond Earth.

Our specific objectives include:

  • Increasing awareness of the scientific challenges associated with extraterrestrial environments.
  • Introducing fundamental concepts related to agriculture, plant biology, and sustainable food production.
  • Encouraging interest in science, technology, engineering, and mathematics (STEM).
  • Promoting critical thinking, experimentation, and problem-solving.
  • Demonstrating the importance of responsible resource management.
  • Exploring the relationship between technological innovation and environmental sustainability.
  • Making scientific education more accessible through interactive digital experiences.

Through these objectives, SpaceFarm seeks to establish a meaningful connection between entertainment and education.

4. How Does It Work?

SpaceFarm was developed with the purpose of educating younger generations through interactive and immersive gameplay, combining agricultural science, space exploration, and technology.

It transforms complex scientific concepts into practical experiences, allowing players to learn through experimentation, exploration, and problem-solving within a simulated extraterrestrial environment.

The game is designed around several interconnected mechanics, including resource management, agricultural development, environmental adaptation, and scientific exploration.

Players are introduced to the challenges of operating in environments where the conditions necessary for human survival and plant growth differ significantly from those found on Earth.

Through agricultural activities, players explore the importance of water, nutrients, temperature, light, and controlled growing environments.

Resource management introduces the necessity of making responsible decisions when essential materials and supplies are limited.

Environmental challenges encourage players to understand how planetary conditions influence technological and agricultural development.

The game also incorporates educational concepts inspired by real scientific research, allowing players to establish connections between their actions and the principles behind sustainable space exploration.

Rather than presenting information exclusively through written explanations, SpaceFarm integrates scientific concepts into the gameplay itself.

This allows players to develop knowledge progressively while remaining actively involved in the experience.

Ultimately, SpaceFarm seeks to demonstrate how scientific understanding, technological innovation, and responsible decision-making can contribute to addressing the challenges of sustaining life beyond Earth.

5. Scientific Background

5.1 Agriculture Beyond Earth

Agriculture is one of the fundamental systems required to support long-duration human space exploration.

While transporting food from Earth is possible for certain missions, establishing sustainable food production systems could become increasingly important for extended operations on the Moon or Mars.

Plants can contribute to space habitats by providing food and participating in biological processes associated with oxygen production and carbon dioxide consumption.

However, cultivating plants beyond Earth presents significant scientific and technological challenges.

Unlike terrestrial environments, extraterrestrial locations may lack naturally suitable growing conditions.

As a result, agricultural systems must account for factors such as atmospheric composition, water availability, temperature regulation, radiation protection, and nutrient delivery.

SpaceFarm introduces these concepts through simulated agricultural activities, helping players understand why growing food in space requires carefully designed systems.

5.2 Environmental Conditions on Mars

Mars represents an important destination for scientific exploration because of its geological history, environmental characteristics, and potential relevance to future human missions.

Nevertheless, its surface presents conditions that make conventional agriculture impractical without substantial technological support.

Mars has an extremely thin atmosphere composed primarily of carbon dioxide, significantly lower atmospheric pressure than Earth, and generally cold surface temperatures.

Its surface is also exposed to elevated radiation levels compared with Earth's surface because it lacks a thick protective atmosphere and a global magnetic field comparable to Earth's.

Additionally, Martian regolith differs from fertile terrestrial soil and may contain compounds that create challenges for plant cultivation.

These environmental characteristics demonstrate why agricultural development on Mars would require controlled environments and specialized technologies.

SpaceFarm uses these scientific challenges as inspiration for educational gameplay.

5.3 Water and Resource Management

Water is essential for biological processes, agricultural production, and human survival.

In extraterrestrial environments, obtaining, conserving, and recycling water would be critical for sustainable operations.

Future space habitats may depend on advanced water recovery systems and efficient agricultural techniques to reduce resource consumption.

SpaceFarm introduces resource management as an educational concept, encouraging players to recognize the importance of conservation and efficient decision-making.

These principles are also relevant to environmental sustainability on Earth, where water availability and agricultural efficiency remain major global concerns.

5.4 Controlled Agricultural Environments

Because the surface of Mars does not naturally provide suitable conditions for conventional crop cultivation, future agricultural systems would likely require protected and carefully regulated environments.

Potential approaches include controlled-environment agriculture, hydroponics, and other cultivation systems designed to regulate water, nutrients, lighting, and atmospheric conditions.

These technologies are relevant to ongoing research into food production for space missions.

By introducing players to the principles behind controlled agricultural environments, SpaceFarm connects gameplay with scientific challenges associated with future space exploration.

6. What Benefits Does SpaceFarm Provide?

SpaceFarm aims to address gaps in basic scientific knowledge related to space exploration, extraterrestrial environments, and the role of agriculture in future space missions.

By combining entertainment with science-based educational content, it provides an accessible way for younger generations to develop an understanding of subjects that are often considered complex or difficult to approach.

One of its primary benefits is encouraging learning through direct interaction.

Instead of simply presenting scientific information, the game allows players to explore agricultural systems, manage limited resources, understand environmental conditions, and discover how these factors influence the possibility of sustaining life beyond Earth.

Additionally, the project promotes critical thinking, problem-solving, creativity, and environmental awareness.

It introduces players to the importance of sustainable resource management and the potential of agricultural technology in addressing future challenges, both on Earth and in space.

Another significant benefit is its accessibility.

By developing SpaceFarm using web technologies, we aim to provide an educational experience that can be accessed through compatible web browsers without requiring specialized gaming hardware.

This approach has the potential to make the game suitable for educational environments, independent learning, and introductory scientific activities.

Ultimately, our goal is to make scientific education more engaging and accessible, inspiring younger generations to develop an interest in science, technology, engineering, and agriculture while exploring the possibilities of humanity's future beyond our planet.

7. Intended Impact

The intended impact of SpaceFarm extends beyond entertainment.

We aim to contribute to the development of a generation that is more informed, curious, and interested in scientific exploration.

By introducing complex concepts through interactive gameplay, our project seeks to reduce the perceived difficulty of learning about space science and agricultural technology.

We believe that early exposure to scientific subjects can encourage students to explore educational and professional opportunities related to STEM disciplines.

Additionally, SpaceFarm highlights the relationship between space exploration and challenges currently affecting Earth.

Technologies developed to improve resource efficiency, water conservation, and controlled-environment agriculture may also have applications in terrestrial sustainability.

Through this connection, players can recognize that research into extraterrestrial environments is not exclusively concerned with distant planets but can also contribute to technological progress on Earth.

In the long term, we envision SpaceFarm as an expandable educational platform that could introduce additional planetary environments, scientific challenges, and agricultural technologies.

Our broader ambition is to inspire curiosity and demonstrate that scientific discovery can begin with accessible, engaging educational experiences.

8. Development Tools and Technologies

The development of SpaceFarm involved a combination of programming languages, artificial intelligence tools, and digital design software.

Each technology contributed to a different aspect of the development process.

8.1 HTML

HTML was used to establish the structural foundation of the game.

As a standard technology for web development, HTML allowed us to organize the elements required for an interactive browser-based experience.

Its integration with JavaScript provided the foundation for implementing gameplay systems and displaying interactive content.

8.2 JavaScript

JavaScript served as one of the primary programming languages used during development.

It was responsible for implementing interactive functionality and coordinating the logic behind different gameplay systems.

By using JavaScript, our team could develop an interactive experience within a web-based environment while maintaining flexibility for future modifications and improvements.

8.3 ChatGPT

ChatGPT was used as an artificial intelligence tool to support different stages of the development process.

It assisted our team with brainstorming, organizing ideas, understanding programming concepts, identifying potential solutions to technical challenges, and improving project documentation.

It also served as a supporting resource for exploring different approaches to implementing gameplay mechanics and organizing the project's educational content.

8.4 CloudAI

CloudAI was incorporated as an additional artificial intelligence tool to support the development workflow.

It contributed to our use of AI-assisted resources during the creation and organization of the project.

Together with other digital tools, it helped expand the resources available to our team throughout development.

8.5 Aseprite — Pixel Art Editor

Aseprite was used to create and edit the visual assets that establish SpaceFarm's artistic identity.

Through pixel art, we developed and refined graphical elements intended to represent characters, environments, objects, and other visual components of the game.

The pixel art approach allowed us to establish a recognizable visual style while maintaining a relatively lightweight graphical design.

This artistic direction also supports the project's educational purpose by presenting scientific environments in a visually approachable format.

8.6 Cloud-Based Tools

Cloud-based tools supported different aspects of our development workflow, providing resources for organizing and managing project materials.

These technologies contributed to the coordination of programming, design, and documentation activities.

The combination of these technologies allowed our team to integrate programming, artificial intelligence, and digital illustration into a unified educational project.

By using accessible development tools, we were able to transform our initial concept into an interactive experience while exploring different approaches to digital education and game development.

9. Creativity and Innovation

One of the defining characteristics of SpaceFarm is its combination of scientific education and interactive entertainment.

Although space exploration and agricultural simulation are established themes in video games, our project seeks to connect them through an educational experience focused on the scientific challenges of sustaining life beyond Earth.

Instead of treating agriculture as a purely recreational activity, we present it as a system influenced by environmental conditions, resource availability, and technological limitations.

This approach encourages players to consider the scientific principles behind their decisions.

SpaceFarm also emphasizes the relationship between extraterrestrial agriculture and sustainability.

By introducing resource management and environmental adaptation, we aim to demonstrate how challenges associated with space exploration can encourage broader discussions about efficient resource use.

Another creative aspect is our use of pixel art.

Rather than relying on highly detailed graphics, we selected a visual style that prioritizes clarity, accessibility, and consistency.

This approach allows us to present scientific concepts through an approachable game environment.

Furthermore, our decision to develop the game using web technologies reflects our intention to make the experience accessible through commonly available digital platforms.

SpaceFarm's innovation lies primarily in its educational integration: connecting scientific concepts with interactive decisions in a way that encourages players to learn through experience.

10. Factors Considered During Development

Throughout the development process, our team considered several factors to ensure that SpaceFarm remained aligned with its educational objectives.

10.1 Scientific Accuracy

One of our primary considerations was maintaining a connection between the game's educational content and established scientific principles.

Because the project addresses space exploration and agriculture, we recognized the importance of distinguishing realistic scientific challenges from simplified gameplay representations.

Our intention is not to reproduce every aspect of extraterrestrial agriculture with complete scientific precision, but to introduce its fundamental principles in an understandable way.

10.2 Accessibility

We considered the importance of creating an experience that younger audiences could understand without requiring advanced scientific knowledge.

This influenced our decisions regarding gameplay complexity, visual presentation, and the integration of educational information.

10.3 Educational Value

We wanted SpaceFarm to provide more than entertainment.

For this reason, we focused on connecting gameplay activities with concepts related to agriculture, environmental conditions, and sustainable resource management.

10.4 Technical Feasibility

Our team also considered the technical limitations associated with developing an interactive game using the tools and resources available to us.

We prioritized technologies that allowed us to implement core functionality while maintaining the possibility of future improvements.

10.5 Visual Design

The game's pixel art style was selected to create a consistent and approachable visual identity.

We considered how visual simplicity could support navigation, recognition of objects, and interaction with the game environment.

10.6 Sustainability

Environmental sustainability was another important consideration.

Although SpaceFarm focuses on extraterrestrial environments, many of its underlying concepts are relevant to challenges on Earth.

By emphasizing resource conservation and agricultural efficiency, we aim to encourage players to reflect on the importance of sustainable practices.

11. Challenges and Limitations

Developing an educational video game involves balancing scientific accuracy, technical functionality, and player engagement.

One of our main challenges was determining how to represent complex scientific processes through gameplay without making the experience unnecessarily difficult.

Concepts such as environmental regulation, resource management, and extraterrestrial agriculture involve numerous variables that cannot always be represented in full detail within a simplified game.

Another challenge involved integrating the visual and technical components of the project into a consistent experience.

Developing graphical assets, implementing interactive mechanics, and organizing the game's structure required coordination between different stages of development.

We also recognized that an educational simulation cannot fully reproduce the complexity of real extraterrestrial environments.

For this reason, SpaceFarm should be understood as an introductory educational experience rather than a scientifically validated model for planning actual space missions.

These limitations provide opportunities for future improvements, including more detailed environmental systems, expanded educational content, and additional gameplay mechanics.

12. Future Development

Our long-term vision is to expand SpaceFarm into a more comprehensive educational experience.

Future development could introduce additional planetary environments, more advanced agricultural systems, and new scientific challenges.

Potential improvements include the simulation of different atmospheric conditions, more detailed resource management systems, and expanded explanations of the technologies used in controlled-environment agriculture.

We also envision incorporating additional educational activities that allow players to explore concepts related to planetary science, environmental engineering, and sustainable habitat development.

Another potential direction involves introducing progressive learning objectives, allowing players to encounter increasingly complex scientific challenges as they advance through the game.

These improvements could help transform SpaceFarm into a broader educational platform that supports learning across multiple scientific disciplines.

Our objective is to continue developing the experience while maintaining its central purpose: making science accessible through interactive learning.

13. Connection to NASA's Mission

SpaceFarm aligns with broader educational and scientific interests associated with space exploration.

NASA conducts research into the challenges of long-duration human spaceflight, including life-support technologies, resource utilization, and biological systems relevant to future exploration missions.

Understanding how plants grow under different environmental conditions is an important research area for supporting future space exploration.

Our game draws inspiration from these scientific challenges and translates them into an educational experience designed for younger audiences.

By introducing players to the importance of agriculture, environmental adaptation, and sustainable resource management, we aim to encourage interest in subjects connected to ongoing space research.

The project also supports the spirit of the NASA Space Apps Challenge by applying technology, creativity, and scientific knowledge to an educational challenge.

Through this initiative, we hope to demonstrate how accessible digital tools can be used to communicate scientific ideas and inspire interest in future exploration.

14. Conclusion

SpaceFarm represents an effort to connect scientific education, technological development, and interactive entertainment through a shared objective: inspiring younger generations to explore the possibilities of science.

By combining extraterrestrial agriculture, space exploration, and resource management within an educational video game, we aim to transform complex scientific concepts into accessible learning experiences.

The project demonstrates how web technologies, digital art, and artificial intelligence tools can support the development of educational resources.

More importantly, it highlights the value of encouraging curiosity, experimentation, and critical thinking.

As humanity continues to investigate the challenges of exploring and potentially sustaining human life beyond Earth, scientific education will remain essential for preparing future generations.

Through SpaceFarm, we hope to contribute to that educational process by making scientific knowledge more approachable, engaging, and meaningful.

Our vision is to inspire the next generation to understand that the future of space exploration begins with curiosity, education, and the willingness to discover what lies beyond our planet.
